latest_release.name: v1.2.1
latest_release.body:
## [1.2.1] - 2026-11-25

## Fixed
- MTA: in a cluster, an in-memory store error while locking a queued message now retries within seconds instead of parking the message for ten minutes.
- IMAP:
  - IDLE no longer sends unsolicited `FETCH` responses for newly arrived messages, which made Thunderbird and Evolution skip messages announced by `EXISTS` while another command was running.
  - Mailbox names and other strings containing CR or LF are sent as literals, so a shared mailbox name can no longer inject response lines into another user's session.
- JMAP:
  - `/get` methods list an id requested more than once only once in `list` or `notFound`.
  - `Mailbox/set` refuses two sibling mailboxes with the same name created or renamed in the same request.
  - `Email/set` rejects with `invalidPatch` a keyword or mailbox pointer deeper than one level, and an update that both replaces and patches `keywords` or `mailboxIds`.
- Sieve:
  - JMAP reports invalid scripts as `invalidSieve`, a `require` of an unsupported extension is refused, invalid header names in tests no longer fail compilation, and imap4flags variable names require `variables`.
  - `redirect` keeps an empty envelope sender (`MAIL FROM:<>`), and `reject` sends a failure MDN instead of a DSN; `ereject` still produces a DSN. Mail rules now reject with `ereject` (protocol-level refusal) instead of `reject`.
- Calendar: iMIP invitation and update emails now label UTC and fixed-offset times that have no `TZID` with their time zone.
- Exchange:
  - MAPI: Outlook in cached mode no longer shows an empty body for messages whose HTML part is larger than 32 KiB; properties over 32 KiB are now included in cached-mode downloads and FastTransfer copies.
  - EWS: folders now return the `PR_ENTRYID` and `PR_ATTR_HIDDEN` extended properties when requested, which Apple Mail needs to sync the folder list without crashing.
  - ActiveSync: Find reads its search text as KQL, so iOS Mail server searches such as `from:"name" OR subject:"name"` find messages again.
  - ActiveSync: SendMail, SmartReply and SmartForward accept a raw `message/rfc822` body at every protocol version, so Outlook for iOS and Android can send mail.
  - ActiveSync: refused SendMail, SmartReply and SmartForward requests, and requests refused for their body type or invalid WBXML, are logged as `http.error` (debug) with the command, the ActiveSync status and the reason.
  - ActiveSync: a calendar Add with an empty `Recurrence` element is stored as a single event instead of failing with status 6, so iOS Calendar can create events again.
- Auth: password logins on a domain served by an OpenID Connect directory now fail as invalid credentials (`535 5.7.8` over SMTP) and count toward the authentication auto-ban.
- Security:
  - `x:AppPassword/set` and `x:ApiKey/set` only update or delete credentials of their own type, so an app password or API key can no longer change the account password or remove its TOTP.
  - S/MIME key harvesting limits the nesting of the signed content, so a crafted signed message can no longer crash the server with a stack overflow.
  - `Mailbox/set` requires the share right for pointer patches into `shareWith`, so a sharee without `mayShare` can no longer change a mailbox's permissions.
- Store maintenance: a trace retention longer than the time since 2021-09-22 no longer fails the task with "Invalid id cutoff for global unindex".
- In-memory store: when the configured store is not available (for example Stalwart Keep was unreachable at startup), operations now fail with "not configured" and point to the startup log instead of "Operation not supported by store".


<hr />

### Check binary attestation [here](https://github.com/stalwartlabs/stalwart/attestations/72465056)

detail.readme:
Secure, scalable mail & collaboration server with comprehensive protocol support 🛡️
(IMAP, JMAP, SMTP, CalDAV, CardDAV, WebDAV, Microsoft Exchange)


     

   

## Features **Stalwart** is an open-source mail & collaboration server with JMAP, IMAP4, POP3, SMTP, CalDAV, CardDAV, WebDAV and Microsoft Exchange support and a wide range of modern features. It is written in Rust and designed to be secure, fast, robust and scalable. Key features: - **Email** server with complete protocol support: - JMAP: * [JMAP for Mail](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8621) server. * [JMAP for Sieve Scripts](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9661.html). * [JMAP Object Metadata](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-jmap-metadata-04) for e-mails, mailboxes, calendars, contacts, files and Sieve scripts. * [WebSocket](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8887), [Blob Management](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9404.html) and [Quotas](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9425.html) extensions. - IMAP: * [IMAP4rev2](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9051) and [IMAP4rev1](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3501) server. * [ManageSieve](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5804) server. * Numerous [extensions](https://stalw.art/docs/development/rfcs#imap4-and-extensions) supported. - POP3: - [POP3](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc1939) server. - [STLS](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc2595) and [SASL](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5034) support as well as other [extensions](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc2449). - SMTP: * SMTP server with built-in [DMARC](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7489), [DKIMv2](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-dkim-dkim2-spec/) (including post-quantum signatures), [DKIMv1](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6376), [SPF](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7208) and [ARC](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8617) support for message authentication. * Strong transport security through [DANE](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6698), [MTA-STS](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8461) and [SMTP TLS](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8460) reporting. * Automated DKIM key rotation and management. * Inbound throttling and filtering with granular configuration rules, sieve scripting, MTA hooks and milter integration. * Distributed virtual queues with delayed delivery, priority delivery, quotas, routing rules and throttling support. * Envelope rewriting and message modification. - Microsoft Exchange (drop-in replacement for Outlook and ActiveSync clients): * [MAPI over HTTP](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/exchange_server_protocols/ms-oxcmapihttp/d502edcf-0b22-42f2-8500-019f00d60245) for classic Outlook for Windows, in cached and online mode. * Exchange Web Services (EWS) for Outlook for Mac and Apple Mail, Calendar and Contacts. * [Exchange ActiveSync](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/exchange_server_protocols/ms-ashttp/4cbf28dc-2876-41c6-9d87-ba9db86cd40d) 14.1 and 16.1 for phones and tablets. * Autodiscover, global address list and offline address book. - **Collaboration** server: - Calendaring and scheduling: - [CalDAV](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc4791) and [CalDAV Scheduling](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6638) support. - [JMAP for Calendars](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-jmap-calendars-32) support. - Contact management: - [CardDAV](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6352) support. - [JMAP for Contacts](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9610) support. - File storage: - [WebDAV](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc4918) support. - [JMAP for File Storage](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-jmap-filenode-17) support. - Sharing with fine-grained access controls: - [WebDAV ACL](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3744) support. - [JMAP Sharing](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9670) support. - **Spam** and **Phishing** built-in filter: - Comprehensive set of filtering **rules** on par with popular solutions. - AI spam classifier with support for OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, Google Gemini and Ollama models. - Statistical **spam classifier** with collaborative filtering, automatic training capabilities and address book integration. - DNS Blocklists (**DNSBLs**) checking of IP addresses, domains, and hashes. - Collaborative digest-based spam filtering with **Pyzor**. - **Phishing** protection against homographic URL attacks, sender spoofing and other techniques. - Trusted **reply** tracking to recognize and prioritize genuine e-mail replies. - Sender **reputation** monitoring by IP address, ASN, domain and email address. - **Greylisting** to temporarily defer unknown senders. - **Spam traps** to set up decoy email addresses that catch and analyze spam. - **Flexible**: - Pluggable storage backends with **RocksDB**, **FoundationDB**, **PostgreSQL**, **mySQL**, **SQLite**, **S3-Compatible**, **Azure** and **Redis** support. - Full-text search available in 17 languages using the built-in search engine or via **Meilisearch**, **ElasticSearch**, **OpenSearch**, **PostgreSQL** or **mySQL** backends. - Text extraction and indexing of **PDF**, **Microsoft Office**, **OpenDocument**, **EPUB** and **RTF** documents. - Sieve scripting language with support for all [registered extensions](https://www.iana.org/assignments/sieve-extensions/sieve-extensions.xhtml). - Email aliases, mailing lists, subaddressing and catch-all addresses support. - Automated DNS management. - Automatic account configuration and discovery with [PACC](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-mailmaint-pacc/), [autoconfig](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-mailmaint-autoconfig/) and [autodiscover](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/exchange/architecture/client-access/autodiscover?view=exchserver-2019) for Exchange and Outlook clients. - Multi-tenancy support with domain and tenant isolation. - Disk quotas per user and tenant. - **Encryption** with **OpenPGP** and **S/MIME**: - Encryption at rest of each user's mailbox with their own OpenPGP key or S/MIME certificate. - Encryption gateway that encrypts outgoing mail for remote recipients, with opportunistic or required policies and no software needed on the sender's side. - Recipient key discovery from Web Key Directory, keys.openpgp.org, HKP keyservers and DNSSEC-validated OPENPGPKEY and SMIMEA records. - Key harvesting from S/MIME signatures and Autocrypt headers of authenticated incoming mail. - S/MIME certificate validation with bundled root certificates, custom trust anchors and revocation lists. - Post-quantum encryption with ML-KEM for both OpenPGP ([RFC 9980](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9980)) and S/MIME ([RFC 9936](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9936)). - OpenPGP v4 and v6 keys with RSA, ECDH (NIST P-256, P-384, P-521, Curve25519), X25519 and X448, and AES-OCB or AES-GCM authenticated encryption ([RFC 9580](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9580)). - S/MIME with RSA (PKCS #1 v1.5 and RSA-OAEP), ECDH (NIST P-256, P-384, P-521), X25519 and X448 certificates, and AES-CBC or AES-GCM content encryption. - [Header protection](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9788) with Subject hiding. - **Secure and robust**: - Automatic TLS certificate provisioning with [ACME](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8555) using `TLS-ALPN-01`, `DNS-01`, `DNS-PERSIST-01` or `HTTP-01` challenges. - Blob store encryption with server-held AES-256-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305 keys, with key rotation and re-encryption of stored data. - Automated blocking of IP addresses that attack, abuse or scan the server for exploits. - SSRF protection for outbound requests. - Rate limiting. - Security audited (read the [report](https://stalw.art/blog/security-audit)). - Memory safe (thanks to Rust). - **Scalable and fault-tolerant**: - Designed to handle growth seamlessly, from small setups to large-scale deployments of thousands of nodes. - Built with **fault tolerance** and **high availability** in mind, recovers from hardware or software failures with minimal operational impact. - Peer-to-peer cluster coordination or with **Kafka**, **Redpanda**, **NATS** or **Redis**. - **Kubernetes**, **Apache Mesos** and **Docker Swarm** support for automated scaling and container orchestration. - Read replicas, sharded blob storage and in-memory data stores for high performance and low latency. - Tiered caching with snapshots that can be swapped to disk, Redis or the blob store. - **Authentication and Authorization**: - **OpenID Connect** authentication. - OAuth 2.0 authorization with [authorization code](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8628) and [device authorization](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8628) flows. - OAuth scopes, connected applications management and [Client ID Metadata Documents](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-oauth-client-id-metadata-document/). - **LDAP**, **OIDC**, **SQL** or built-in authentication backend support. - System for Cross-domain Identity Management ([SCIM](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc7643/)) v2 for automated provisioning. - Two-factor authentication with Time-based One-Time Passwords (`2FA-TOTP`) - Passkeys ([WebAuthn](https://www.w3.org/TR/webauthn-3/)) for passwordless, phishing-resistant sign-in. - Application passwords (App Passwords). - Roles and permissions. - Access Control Lists (ACLs). - **Observability**: - Logging and tracing with **OpenTelemetry**, journald, log files and console support. - Metrics with **OpenTelemetry** and **Prometheus** integration. - Webhooks for event-driven automation. - Alerts with email and webhook notifications. - Live tracing and metrics. - **Web-based administration**: - Dashboard with real-time statistics and monitoring. - Account, domain, group and mailing list management. - SMTP queue management for messages and outbound DMARC and TLS reports. - Report visualization interface for received DMARC, TLS-RPT and Failure (ARF) reports. - Configuration of every aspect of the mail server. - Log viewer with search and filtering capabilities. - Self-service portal for password reset and encryption-at-rest key management. ## Screenshots ## Presentation Whether you are evaluating options, presenting Stalwart to your team or your boss, or just curious about how it works under the hood, the [slides](https://stalw.art/slides) walk you through its key features, architecture and benefits. ## Get Started Install Stalwart on your server by following the instructions for your platform: - [Linux / MacOS / FreeBSD](https://stalw.art/docs/install/platform/linux) - [Windows](https://stalw.art/docs/install/platform/windows) - [Docker](https://stalw.art/docs/install/platform/docker) All documentation is available at [stalw.art/docs](https://stalw.art/docs/install/get-started). ## Where do I get support? If you run into a problem, find a bug or have a question, head to the [Stalwart Support Portal](https://support.stalw.art). It is free for everyone, and our team answers. Organizations that need more can purchase an [Enterprise license](https://stalw.art/enterprise) for priority support from Stalwart Labs LLC, with response-time commitments and a private Priority Support area on the portal. ## Why isn't everything AGPL? About 85% of Stalwart's features are free and open source under the AGPL-3.0. The rest make up the [Enterprise edition](https://stalw.art/enterprise/), and are mostly features that matter to large organizations and hosting providers running Stalwart at scale, such as multi-tenancy, SCIM provisioning, sharded storage and live telemetry. The full breakdown is on the [comparison page](https://stalw.art/compare/). Stalwart is built by a full-time professional team, not as a side project, and open source sponsorship covers only a small fraction of what that costs. Enterprise subscriptions pay for the work that every Stalwart user benefits from: - The engineers who maintain and extend the Community edition, with a new release every week. - Security fixes within 24 hours of a report, and an independent security audit every time a large part of Stalwart is rewritten. - Free community support at [support.stalw.art](https://support.stalw.art). - Stress tests and benchmarks on dozens of cloud servers at a time across many regions. - Work on email standards at the IETF, where we are the authors of multiple Internet-Drafts in progress. The Community edition is complete and open source, and it will stay that way: - Stalwart remains licensed under the AGPL-3.0. - No existing open source feature will ever be moved to the Enterprise edition. - Most new features go to the Community edition. If you find Stalwart useful, there are two ways to help keep it free. If your organization needs Enterprise features, [subscribe to the Enterprise edition](https://stalw.art/pricing/). Otherwise, you can [become a sponsor on OpenCollective](https://opencollective.com/stalwart): sponsors who contribute $5 per month or more automatically receive an Enterprise license, and those who contribute $30 per month or more also get access to [Premium Support](https://stalw.art/support) from Stalwart Labs. Thank you! ## How can I contribute? Contributions are welcome, with a few rules that keep the project maintainable: - Because of the high volume of low-quality, AI-generated submissions, only vouched contributors can open pull requests. To be added to the list, post at [support.stalw.art](https://support.stalw.art) describing the change you would like to submit, with a link to it. - For now, only bug fixes and translations are accepted. New features are not, unless they are just a few lines of code. The full guidelines are in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). You can also help without writing code: report bugs, answer questions on the support portal, or tell others about Stalwart. ## Funding Part of the development of this project was funded through: - [NGI0 Entrust Fund](https://nlnet.nl/entrust), a fund established by [NLnet](https://nlnet.nl/) with financial support from the European Commission's [Next Generation Internet](https://ngi.eu/) programme, under the aegis of DG Communications Networks, Content and Technology under grant agreement No 101069594. - [NGI Zero Core](https://nlnet.nl/NGI0/), a fund established by [NLnet](https://nlnet.nl/) with financial support from the European Commission's programme, under the aegis of DG Communications Networks, Content and Technology under grant agreement No 101092990. ## License This project is dual-licensed under the **GNU Affero General Public License v3.0** (AGPL-3.0; as published by the Free Software Foundation) and the **Stalwart Enterprise License v2 (SELv2)**: - The [GNU Affero General Public License v3.0](./LICENSES/AGPL-3.0-only.txt) is a free software license that ensures your freedom to use, modify, and distribute the software, with the condition that any modified versions of the software must also be distributed under the same license. - The [Stalwart Enterprise License v2 (SELv2)](./LICENSES/LicenseRef-SEL.txt) is a proprietary license designed for commercial use.
